# Supabase trigger ownership error (2026-01-31 15:16Z)

_**User**_

Fix

Problem summary
Error "ERROR: 42501: must be owner of relation users" means the role executing CREATE FUNCTION / CREATE TRIGGER does not own the target relation (public.users). In Postgres only the owner of a table (or a superuser) can create a trigger on it or create objects that implicitly require ownership checks.

You created a SECURITY DEFINER function in schema public that inserts into public.users and then attempted to create a trigger on auth.users. The failing statement is likely the CREATE TRIGGER on auth.users (or possibly the CREATE FUNCTION in public if ownership checks involve the target table). The DB is telling you the active role running the migration isn't owner of the relation "users" (public.users).

Why this happens on Supabase
Supabase's auth schema and many public objects are owned by different roles (e.g., supabase_admin / pg_database_owner / postgres). Your migration is likely running as a less-privileged role (the dashboard migration role or the project owner role that isn't table owner).
Creating a trigger on auth.users is allowed only to the owner of auth.users. Creating a trigger referencing a function in another schema may also require ownership or suitable privileges.
Fix options (pick one)
Run the migration as the owner (recommended for schema changes)
Connect and run the migration as the DB role that owns auth.users (likely supabase_admin or the original owner). On Supabase you can run SQL as the project owner using the SQL editor in the dashboard or using a service_role key that has permission to run DDL.
If you use the SQL editor in Supabase Dashboard it typically runs as the owner; try there.
Change ownership temporarily
Have the current owner (or an admin) run: ALTER TABLE public.users OWNER TO your_migration_role; -- run your migration ALTER TABLE public.users OWNER TO previous_owner; This requires admin access and is not recommended in production.
Create the trigger in the same schema as the table and ensure owner matches
Ensure the migration runs under the owner of auth.users if creating trigger on auth.users. For example, create the trigger function in the auth schema and then create trigger as the auth.users owner:
Create function auth.handle_new_auth_user() SECURITY DEFINER ...;
CREATE TRIGGER ... ON auth.users ... EXECUTE FUNCTION auth.handle_new_auth_user(); Note: moving the function into auth schema may be preferable because the owner of auth schema/tables will already be the owner. But you must ensure no security exposures; keep SECURITY DEFINER and revoke execute from anon/authenticated if appropriate.
Use a SECURITY DEFINER function owned by the table owner
Create the function as the owner of auth.users (or set its owner to that role). Only the owner can set an object owner. Example workflow:
As owner: CREATE FUNCTION auth.handle_new_auth_user() SECURITY DEFINER ...;
As owner: CREATE TRIGGER ... ON auth.users ...; This avoids the "must be owner" check.
Suggested minimal change (safe approach)
Move the function into the auth schema and run the migration as a privileged role (SQL editor). Example changes you'll need:
create function auth.handle_new_auth_user() ... (instead of public.handle_new_auth_user)
create trigger on auth.users AFTER INSERT ... execute function auth.handle_new_auth_user();
Keep SECURITY DEFINER on the function and, after creation, REVOKE EXECUTE FROM anon, authenticated if you don't want public to call it.
If you want, I can:

Provide the exact SQL adjusted to create the function in auth schema and with revokes (I will not run it; I'll generate it for you), or
Attempt to run a statement that checks ownership (who owns public.users and auth.users) so we confirm owners (I can run SQL now).

        "contents": "-- Enable realtime publication for users table\nalter publication supabase_realtime add table public.users;\n\n-- Create trigger function for realtime broadcasting on users table\n-- Uses realtime.broadcast_changes for database change notifications\ncreate or replace function public.users_realtime_broadcast_trigger()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\nbegin\n  -- Broadcast changes to users table using dedicated topic pattern\n  -- Topic format: users:{user_id} for user-specific updates\n  perform realtime.broadcast_changes(\n    tg_table_name || ':' || coalesce(new.id, old.id)::text,\n    tg_op,\n    tg_op,\n    tg_table_name,\n    tg_table_schema,\n    new,\n    old\n  );\n  return coalesce(new, old);\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.users_realtime_broadcast_trigger() is 'Trigger function that broadcasts changes to the users table via Supabase Realtime. Uses dedicated topic pattern users:{user_id}.';\n\n-- Create trigger for realtime broadcasting on users table\ncreate trigger users_realtime_broadcast_trigger\nafter insert or update or delete on public.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.users_realtime_broadcast_trigger();\n\n-- Create indexes for common queries\ncreate index profiles_user_id_idx on public.profiles(user_id);\ncreate index profiles_work_email_idx on public.profiles(work_email);\ncreate index profiles_team_id_idx on public.profiles(team_id);\ncreate index users_google_email_idx on public.users(google_email);\ncreate index users_suggested_work_email_idx on public.users(suggested_work_email);\ncreate index users_auth_user_id_idx on public.users(auth_user_id);\n\n-- Enable Row Level Security on all tables\nalter table public.users enable row level security;\nalter table public.profiles enable row level security;\nalter table public.teams enable row level security;\n\n-- RLS Policies for users table\n-- Users can view their own user record (via auth_user_id link to auth.users)\ncreate policy \"Users can view their own user record\" on public.users\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) );",

        "contents": "-- Migration: Create users, profiles, and teams schema with realtime support\n-- Purpose: Creates custom users table (replacing auth.users reference), profiles table, teams table\n-- Includes automatic updated_at triggers and realtime broadcasting for users table\n-- Affected tables: users, profiles, teams\n-- Special considerations: Users table is separate from auth.users, profiles reference users table\n\n-- Create profile_role enum for profiles table\ncreate type public.profile_role as enum ('student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin');\n\n-- Create users table (custom table, separate from auth.users)\n-- Stores Google OAuth user data and OTP tracking\n-- Linked to auth.users via auth_user_id for authentication checks\ncreate table public.users (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  auth_user_id uuid unique references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\n  google_email text not null unique,\n  suggested_work_email text,\n  google_profile_picture text,\n  google_full_name text,\n  last_otp_sent_at timestamptz,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\ncomment on table public.users is 'Custom users table storing Google OAuth user data and OTP tracking. Separate from auth.users but linked via auth_user_id for authentication.';\n\n-- Create teams table\ncreate table public.teams (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  picture text,\n  color text,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\ncomment on table public.teams is 'Team information for organizing users into groups.';\n\n-- Create profiles table (pre-created by admin, linked to user after verification)\n-- References the new users table instead of auth.users\ncreate table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),",

        "contents": "-- Migration: Restrict signups to Google OAuth only\n-- Purpose: Blocks email/password signups and OTP signups, only allows Google OAuth\n-- This ensures all new accounts must be created via Google OAuth\n\n-- Create before_user_created hook in public schema to only allow Google OAuth signups\n-- Blocks email/password signups and other OAuth providers\n-- Uses public schema instead of auth schema\ncreate or replace function public.before_user_created_hook(event jsonb)\nreturns jsonb\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_provider text;\n  v_encrypted_password text;\n  v_app_metadata jsonb;\n  v_identity jsonb;\n  v_has_google_identity boolean := false;\nbegin\n  -- Extract encrypted_password first (most reliable indicator of password signup)\n  v_encrypted_password := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;&gt;'encrypted_password';\n  \n  -- Block password-based signups immediately (they have encrypted_password)\n  if v_encrypted_password is not null then\n    raise exception 'Password-based signups are not allowed. Please use Google OAuth to sign in.';\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Extract provider from multiple possible locations\n  -- 1. raw_user_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'provider'\n  v_provider := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'raw_user_meta_data'-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  \n  -- 2. app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider'\n  v_app_metadata := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'app_metadata';\n  if v_provider is null and v_app_metadata is not null then\n    v_provider := v_app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  end if;\n  \n  -- 3. Check identities array for Google provider (most reliable for OAuth)\n  if event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities' is not null then\n    for v_identity in \n      select value from jsonb_array_elements(event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities')\n    loop\n      if v_identity-&gt;&gt;'provider' = 'google' then\n        v_has_google_identity := true;\n        exit;\n      end if;\n    end loop;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Allow Google OAuth signups (check both provider variable and identities array)\n  if v_provider = 'google' or v_has_google_identity then\n    return event;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- If we reach here, it's not a Google OAuth signup and not a password signup\n  -- This must be an OTP or other email-based signup attempt",

        "contents": "create table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  picture text,  -- defaults to Google profile picture on link\n  user_id uuid unique references public.users(id) on delete set null,  -- linked after OTP verification\n  work_email text unique not null,\n  role public.profile_role not null default 'student',\n  team_id uuid references public.teams(id) on delete set null,\n  phone_number text,\n  personal_email text,\n  date_of_birth date,\n  removed_access timestamptz,  -- null = active, set = revoked\n  removed_access_by uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete set null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  constraint valid_czu_domain check (\n    work_email like '%@studenti.czu.cz' or work_email like '%@pef.czu.cz'\n  )\n);\n\ncomment on table public.profiles is 'User profile data with role and team membership. Pre-created by admin, linked to user after OTP verification.';\n\n-- Create trigger function to automatically update updated_at column\n-- This function will be used by all tables with updated_at columns\ncreate or replace function public.handle_updated_at()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity invoker\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\nbegin\n  -- Update the updated_at column to current timestamp on any update\n  new.updated_at := now();\n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.handle_updated_at() is 'Trigger function that automatically updates the updated_at column to the current timestamp on row updates.';\n\n-- Create triggers for updated_at on all tables\ncreate trigger users_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\ncreate trigger teams_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.teams\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\ncreate trigger profiles_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.profiles\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\n-- Enable realtime publication for users table\nalter publication supabase_realtime add table public.users;",

        "contents": "create policy \"Users can view their own user record\" on public.users\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) );\n\n-- Users can update their own user record\ncreate policy \"Users can update their own user record\" on public.users\nfor update\nto authenticated\nusing ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) )\nwith check ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) );\n\n-- Allow authenticated users to insert their own user record (during signup)\ncreate policy \"Users can insert their own user record\" on public.users\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( auth_user_id = (select auth.uid()) );\n\n-- RLS Policies for profiles table\n-- Users can view their own profile (via user_id -&gt;     {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./supabase/migrations/20260131000000_validate_czu_email_domain.sql",

        },
        "contents": "  v_email_change text;\n  v_domain text;\nbegin\n  -- Only validate on UPDATE (email changes), not INSERT (new user creation)\n  -- This allows OAuth signups (Google, etc.) to create accounts with any email\n  if tg_op != 'UPDATE' then\n    return NEW;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Validate email_change field (where Supabase stores new email during change process)\n  -- This applies to ALL users (both OAuth and email-only)\n  -- OAuth users can sign up, but when they try to add an email identity, it must be CZU domain\n  if OLD.email_change is distinct from NEW.email_change then\n    v_email_change := NEW.email_change;\n    \n    -- Skip validation if email_change is null or empty\n    if v_email_change is not null and v_email_change != '' then\n      -- Extract domain from email_change (everything after @)\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email_change, '@', 2));\n      \n      -- Validate domain is one of the allowed CZU domains\n      -- This applies to all users, including OAuth users trying to add email identity\n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  -- Validate email field if it changed\n  -- For OAuth users: validate when they're changing from OAuth email to a new email\n  -- For email-only users: always validate\n  if OLD.email is distinct from NEW.email then\n    v_email := NEW.email;\n    \n    -- Skip validation if email is null or empty\n    if v_email is not null and v_email != '' then\n      -- Extract domain from email (everything after @)\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email, '@', 2));\n      \n      -- Validate domain is one of the allowed CZU domains\n      -- This applies to all users when changing primary email\n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  return NEW;\nend;\n$$;\n\n-- Grant execute permission to authenticated and anonymous roles\n-- This allows the trigger to execute when users update their email",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "  v_email_change text;",

          },
          {
            "text": "  v_domain text;",

          },
          {
            "text": "begin",
